column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses singular “my hand” and “I will devote”; BSB uses plural “our hands” and “we will devote.”
The Hebrew says the LORD heard Israel’s “voice” and ends with singular “he called”; BSB uses “plea” and plural “they named.”
The Hebrew names the “Sea of Reeds” and says the people’s soul became short; BSB has “Red Sea” and says the people became impatient.
The Hebrew repeats “bread” and says “our soul loathes”; BSB uses “bread” and then “food” and says “we detest.”
The Hebrew describes “fiery serpents” and actively says the serpents bit the people; BSB has “venomous snakes” and the passive “the Israelites were bitten.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the serpent”; BSB uses plural “the snakes.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “make for yourself”; BSB says “Make.”
The Hebrew actively describes the serpent biting a person; BSB refers passively to anyone “who was bitten.”

The Hebrew uses “toward the rising of the sun”; BSB says “to the east.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew describes the wilderness as extending “from the border” of the Amorite; BSB says it “extends into Amorite territory.”

The Hebrew joins the gathering and giving of water with “and”; BSB uses “so that.”

The Hebrew has singular “scepter” and plural “their staffs”; BSB has plural “their scepters” and “their staffs.”

The Hebrew begins with singular “Let me pass” and then shifts to “we”; BSB uses plural “us” throughout. The Hebrew joins field and vineyard with “and,” where BSB has “or.”
The Hebrew repeats Sihon’s name and says “all his people”; BSB uses a pronoun for the second name and says “his whole army.”
The Hebrew uses “the mouth of the sword”; BSB has “put him to the sword.”
The Hebrew calls the settlements Heshbon’s “daughters”; BSB says “villages.”
The Hebrew explicitly says the territory was taken “from his hand”; BSB omits this image.
The Hebrew says “built” and “established”; BSB uses “rebuilt” and “restored.”
